{"kind":"tool","id":"c4VtwZh1w-Q","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/migrations/0003_folders_files.sql","instructions":"Migration 0003: folders and files with ownership-aware FKs and cycle guard","content":"-- 0003_folders_files.sql
-- Logical folders and files. Ownership is part of every foreign key so a row
-- can never reference another user's parent folder.

create table public.folders (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  parent_folder_id uuid,
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  deleted_at timestamptz,
  constraint folders_name_length check (length(btrim(name)) between 1 and 255),
  constraint folders_not_own_parent check (parent_folder_id is null or parent_folder_id <> id),
  constraint folders_user_id_unique unique (user_id, id),
  constraint folders_parent_same_owner foreign key (user_id, parent_folder_id)
    references public.folders (user_id, id)
    on delete restrict
);

comment on table public.folders is
  'Folder hierarchy. Deleting a folder row is restricted while children exist; '
  'user deletion is soft (deleted_at).';

-- Reject cycles (a folder may not be its own ancestor).
create or replace function public.enforce_folder_hierarchy()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  if new.parent_folder_id is null then
    return new;
  end if;

  if new.parent_folder_id = new.id then
    raise exception 'folder hierarchy cycle: folder cannot be its own parent'
      using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  if exists (
    with recursive ancestors as (
      select f.id, f.parent_folder_id
      from public.folders f
      where f.id = new.parent_folder_id
      union all
      select f.id, f.parent_folder_id
      from public.folders f
      join ancestors a on f.id = a.parent_folder_id
    )
    select 1 from ancestors where id = new.id
  ) then
    raise exception 'folder hierarchy cycle: parent is a descendant of folder'
      using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger folders_enforce_hierarchy
before insert or update of parent_folder_id on public.folders
for each row execute function public.enforce_folder_hierarchy();

create trigger folders_set_updated_at
before update on public.folders
for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

create table public.files (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  folder_id uuid,
  name text not null,
  extension text,
  mime_type text not null,
  logical_size_bytes bigint not null default 0,
  current_version_id uuid,
  content_fingerprint text,
  favorite boolean not null default false,
  description text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  deleted_at timestamptz,
  constraint files_name_length check (length(btrim(name)) between 1 and 255),
  constraint files_logical_size_nonnegative check (logical_size_bytes >= 0),
  constraint files_user_id_unique unique (user_id, id),
  constraint files_folder_same_owner foreign key (user_id, folder_id)
    references public.folders (user_id, id)
    on delete set null (folder_id)
);

comment on table public.files is
  'Logical file records. Physical payloads live in storage_objects via file_versions; '
  'deleting a metadata row never deletes remote provider content.';

create trigger files_set_updated_at
before update on public.files
for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();
"}}

create or replace function public.reject_file_version_mutation()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  raise exception 'file_versions rows are immutable; create a new version instead'
    using errcode = '23514';
end;
$$;

before update on public.file_versions

returns trigger

as $$
begin
  if new.current_version_id is null then
    return new;
  end if;

  if not exists (

    from public.file_versions v
    where v.id = new.current_version_id
      and v.file_id = new.id
      and v.user_id = new.user_id

  constraint tags_user_id_unique unique (user_id, id)

  on public.tags (user_id, lower(btrim(name)));

create table public.file_tags (
  user_id uuid not null,
  file_id uuid not null,

    on delete cascade

create table public.shares (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  file_version_id uuid not null,
  token_hash text not null unique,
  permission text not null default 'read',
  expires_at timestamptz,
  max_downloads integer,
  download_count integer not null default 0,
  password_verifier text,
  revoked_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint shares_permission_check check (permission in ('read')),

    on delete restrict
);

comment on table public.shares is
  'Revocable share of one immutable file version. Only token_hash is stored; the '
  'raw token lives with the recipient. Revocation cannot erase copies already '
  'downloaded. download_count must be incremented atomically.';

  constraint audit_events_event_type_length check (length(btrim(event_type)) between 1 and 120)

comment on table public.audit_events is

alter table public.user_settings enable row level security;
alter table public.storage_connections enable row level security;
alter table public.folders enable row level security;
alter table public.files enable row level security;

alter table public.tags enable row level security;
alter table public.file_tags enable row level security;
alter table public.upload_jobs enable row level security;
alter table public.upload_chunks enable row level security;
alter table public.shares enable row level security;

A self-hostable personal cloud drive. Metadata lives in PostgreSQL (Supabase-compatible),
encrypted payloads are meant to live in **your own** Telegram Saved Messages, and
files are encrypted in the browser so the server never sees plaintext.

The authoritative specification is [SRS & FDD.md](SRS%20%26%20FDD.md).

> **Status: Milestone 1 — foundation.** Authentication, owner-scoped authorization,
> the full database schema with row-level security, the application shell and both
> themes are implemented and tested. Encrypted uploads, Telegram storage, previews,
> versions, sharing and the PWA are **not** implemented yet; the UI never pretends
> otherwise. See [Milestone 1 report](docs/reports/milestone-1.md).

---

## Requirements

- Node.js **20.19+** (developed on 24.x) and pnpm 9+
- No Docker, Telegram account or Supabase project is required for local development

## Quick start

```bash

# 1. Configure the API (generates a local development signing secret)
cp apps/api/.env.example apps/api/.env
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('base64url'))"
#   → paste the value into DEV_AUTH_SECRET

# 2. Configure the web app
cp apps/web/.env.example apps/web/.env.local

# 3. Run the two services (separate terminals)
pnpm dev:api     # http://127.0.0.1:8787  (creates + migrates the local database on boot)
pnp [… 1,080 characters omitted] peScript API
    src/config/        validated environment configuration
    src/database/      driver-agnostic database layer, migration runner
    src/modules/       health, me, setup, dev-auth route modules
    src/security/      token verification (dev + Supabase), identity derivation
    test/              authorization and RLS test suites
  web/                 Next.js App Router
    src/app/           routes: (auth)/sign-in, (app)/home, (app)/settings
    src/components/    layout, ui, dashboard, feedback components
    src/features/      auth, settings, setup feature modules
    src/lib/           API client, session, theme, formatting
packages/
  contracts/           TypeBox schemas shared by API and web
supabase/
  migrations/          0001–0010 schema, constraints, indexes, RLS, checks
  local/               local-only auth stub (never apply to Supabase)
docs/                  setup, decisions and milestone reports
```

## Security model (what exists today)

- **Identity comes only from a verified token.** The API reads the subject from a
  signature-verified JWT; no endpoint accepts a user id from the client. Tokens signed
  with a non end-user role (`service_role`) are rejected.
- **Ownership is part of the schema.** Every user-owned table carries `user_id`, and
  relationships use composite foreign keys `(user_id, …)` so a row can never point at
  another owner's data.
- **Row-level security is enabled on every table**, with `auth.uid()` policies for
  user-facing tables and **no grants at all** for internal tables (storage connections,
  storage objects, upload jobs, upload chunks). `anon` has zero privileges.
- **Migration 0010 fails the build** if RLS is missing, if `anon` gains privileges, or
  if a table reachable by `authenticated` has no policy.
- **Sessions stay out of JavaScript.** The web app stores the access token in an
  httpOnly cookie and attaches it server-side; API responses are `no-store`.
- **Telegram session material is never exposed** by any endpoint and does not exist in
  the database yet.

StackBase runs as two independently deployable services:

| Service | Directory | Default URL |
|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js) | `apps/web` | http://localhost:3000 |
| API (Fastify) | `apps/api` | http://127.0.0.1:8787 |

## 1. Install

```bash
pnpm install
```

Requires Node.js 20.19+ and pnpm 9+.

## 2. API configuration

```bash
cp apps/api/.env.example apps/api/.env
node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('base64url'))"
```

Paste the generated value into `DEV_AUTH_SECRET` in `apps/api/.env`. Every variable is
validated at startup; the process refuses to boot with a clear list of problems.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | `production` disables `AUTH_MODE=dev` |
| `HOST` / `PORT` | `127.0.0.1` / `8787` | `PORT=0` is treated as unset (documented default) |
| `WEB_ORIGIN` | `http://localhost:3000` | CORS allow-list |
| `AUTH_MODE` | `dev` | `dev` or `supabase` |
| `DEV_AUTH_SECRET` | — | Required for `AUTH_MODE=dev`, min 32 chars |
| `DEV_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` | `86400` | 300–2592000 |
| `DATABASE_URL` | empty | Empty ⇒ local PGlite; set ⇒ PostgreSQL/Supabase |
| `STACKBASE_LOCAL_AUTH_STUB` | `0` | Only for a bare PostgreSQL without Supabase's auth schema |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | Pino level; authorization headers [… 1,511 characters omitted] b build
```

- `apps/api/test/auth.test.ts` — token validation, identity derivation, error envelope
- `apps/api/test/setup-status.test.ts` — owner-scoped status, no cross-user leakage
- `apps/api/test/rls.test.ts` — assumes the `authenticated` role and sets
  `request.jwt.claims` exactly as Supabase does, then proves cross-user access fails
- `apps/web/test/*` — formatting and dashboard component rendering

Tests need no external services: each API suite starts an in-memory PostgreSQL, applies
every migration, and disposes of it afterwards.

## Switching to Supabase

1. Create a Supabase project.
2. Apply this repository's migrations to it, in order, with the Supabase CLI:

   ```bash
   supabase link --project-ref <ref>
   supabase db push
   ```

   The migrations reference `auth.users` and `auth.uid()`, which a Supabase project
   already provides. Do **not** apply the local stub.

3. Set the API environment:

   ```env
   AUTH_MODE=supabase
   SUPABASE_URL=https://<ref>.supabase.co
   SUPABASE_JWKSS_URL= # optional; defaults to <SUPABASE_URL>/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json
   SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET= # only for legacy HS256 signing keys
   DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:<password>@db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres
   ```

   The API verifies Supabase access tokens (issuer `<SUPABASE_URL>/auth/v1`, audience
   `authenticated`) against the project's JWKS, or against the legacy JWT secret when one
   is configured. `POST /api/v1/dev/session` is not registered in this mode.

4. The web app needs a Supabase sign-in screen before it can be deployed. Until that
   ships (a later milestone), `AUTH_MODE=dev` is the supported local and self-hosted path.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| `Invalid configuration: DEV_AUTH_SECRET is required` | Paste the generated secret into `apps/api/.env` |
| Web shows "Something went wrong" | The API is not running: start `pnpm dev:api` |
| `Migration failed: schema "auth" does not exist` | You pointed `DATABASE_URL` at a bare PostgreSQL. Use Supabase, or set `STACKBASE_LOCAL_AUTH_STUB=1` knowingly |
| Sign-in returns 404 | The API runs with `AUTH_MODE=supabase` or `NODE_ENV=production`; dev sessions are disabled by design |
| `db:reset` refuses to run | `DATABASE_URL` is set; drop and recreate that database deliberately instead |

- ADR-001 Database driver: PGlite local + pg production; rationale; consequences (single connection, not for concurrent production; production must set DATABASE_URL).
- ADR-002 Auth modes: dev HS256 sessions vs Supabase JWT; dev route gated; production refuses dev mode.
- ADR-003 RLS/grant model: server-only tables have no grants; RLS defense in depth; migration 0010 checks; RLS tests assume authenticated role.
- ADR-004 Identity provisioning via trigger on auth.users, plus defensive idempotent provisioning in /me.
- ADR-005 Theme preference in httpOnly cookie until settings API exists (deviation from storing in user_settings only) — theme column exists, API doesn't update it yet.
- ADR-006 Web session via httpOnly cookie + server-side API calls instead of browser-held Supabase token (interim; when Supabase Auth UI ships, switch to @supabase/ssr cookie session).

{"kind":"tool","id":"c5IStIG_fDE","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/architecture/decisions.md","instructions":"Architecture decision records and documented deviations for milestone 1","content":"# Architecture decisions

Decisions taken while implementing Milestone 1, with the deviations from the SRS/FDD
documented explicitly (SRS final rule 14). Each record states the context, the decision
and the consequences.

---

## ADR-001 — Two database drivers: PGlite locally, `pg` for PostgreSQL/Supabase

**Context.** The spec mandates Supabase PostgreSQL. Local development should not require
Docker, a cloud project or credentials, and the RLS policies are only meaningful when
exercised against a real PostgreSQL engine.

**Decision.** All code talks to a small `Db` interface (`src/database/db.ts`):

- `DATABASE_URL` empty ⇒ **PGlite** (PostgreSQL 17 compiled to WebAssembly) persisted at
  `apps/api/.data/pglite`.
- `DATABASE_URL` set ⇒ **`pg`** pool, for PostgreSQL or Supabase.

Migrations, constraints, triggers and policies are identical in both.

**Consequences.** Local development and the whole test suite run with one command and no
external service. PGlite is a single connection, so it is a development and test driver,
not a production one; concurrent production traffic must set `DATABASE_URL`. Query text
uses `$1` placeholders and no driver-specific extensions, so behavior matches.

---

## ADR-002 — Two auth modes, with dev sessions structurally impossible in production

**Context.** The spec fixes Supabase Auth. There is [… 4,674 characters omitted] ND` (404), `RATE_LIMITED` (429) and `INTERNAL_ERROR`
(500). Validation failures return `VALIDATION_ERROR` with field paths; database outages map
to `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` (503). Stack traces and provider details are never returned.

---

## ADR-008 — RLS tests live with the API suite, not in `supabase/tests`

**Context.** The FDD sketch places database tests in `supabase/tests`. They need the
migration runner, the driver and the test harness, all of which belong to `apps/api`.

**Decision.** `apps/api/test/rls.test.ts` holds the database authorization tests; it reads
`supabase/migrations` directly. `supabase/` stays a pure SQL directory with no Node package.

**Consequences.** One test command, one harness, no duplicated driver setup. The RLS tests
run as the real `authenticated` role with `request.jwt.claims` set the way Supabase does,
so they exercise the policies rather than the API's SQL.

---

## ADR-009 — No client state library yet

**Context.** The FDD prescribes TanStack Query for server state and limited Zustand for
shared UI state. Milestone 1 has no client-side data fetching: every screen is rendered on
the server.

**Decision.** Neither library is installed. Server state is fetched in server components;
interaction state (form pending/error) uses `useActionState`.

**Consequences.** The dependencies arrive with file browsing (Milestone 2), where they are
actually needed; nothing in the current build is dead code.

---

## ADR-010 — `PORT=0` is treated as unset

**Context.** Some toolchains export `PORT=0`, which would bind an ephemeral port that the
web app cannot discover, or fail validation entirely.

**Decision.** `PORT=0` falls back to the documented default (`8787`); any other non-numeric
or out-of-range value is still a configuration error. The API logs the bound address at
startup.

---

## Known gaps at Milestone 1 (deliberate)

- No Telegram MTProto adapter, session storage or `StorageProvider` implementation.
- No cryptographic format, vault key hierarchy or recovery flow; uploads are disabled.
- No upload jobs, chunk transfer or worker process (schema exists, code does not).
- No file/folder/tag/search routes; the schema is in place for Milestone 2.
- No PWA manifest, service worker, offline queue or Playwright end-to-end suite.
- No Dockerfiles or CI pipeline.

**Date:** 25 October 2026
**Scope:** SRS Part E, Milestone 1 (repository inspection, toolchain, Next.js + Fastify
applications, Supabase-auth boundary, migrations and RLS tests, application shell and
themes). Local-first variant agreed up front: no Supabase project and no Telegram
credentials are required to run, test or review this milestone.

## Implemented behavior

**Monorepo and tooling**

- pnpm workspace: `apps/api`, `apps/web`, `packages/contracts`.
- Strict TypeScript everywhere (`pnpm typecheck`), Vitest for all tests.
- Environment configuration is parsed and cross-validated at startup with actionable
  errors (`src/config/env.ts`); no secret has a silent fallback.
- `apps/api/.env.example` and `apps/web/.env.example` document every variable.

**API (Fastify 5, TypeScript)**

- `GET /health` — real database probe; returns `503` and `degraded` when the database is
  unreachable. Response headers: `no-store`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`.
- `GET /api/v1/me` — verified identity, profile and settings; provisions rows
  idempotently if a project predates the trigger.
- `GET /api/v1/setup/status` — owner-scoped storage connection state plus live file,
  folder and byte counts (trashed items excluded).
- `POST /api/v1/dev/session` — development-only local sign-in; never registered in
  production.
- Uniform error envel [… 3,125 characters omitted] ing the "unreachable" and "not connected" states |
| `pnpm --filter @stackbase/api typecheck` | pass |
| `pnpm --filter @stackbase/contracts typecheck` | pass |
| `pnpm --filter @stackbase/web typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) | pass |
| `next build` | pass — `/`, `/settings`, `/sign-in` build as dynamic server-rendered routes |
| Manual browser verification | pass — unauthenticated redirect, sign-in, dashboard with live data, theme switch (aria-pressed + computed colours), settings, sign-out clearing the cookie, mobile layout at 390 px with 56 px touch targets and no horizontal overflow |

`pnpm db:migrate` was run against a fresh database: all ten migrations applied; the
consistency checks in `0010` rejected two genuine defects during development (missing RLS
on the migration bookkeeping table, and a policy-coverage rule that needed to distinguish
server-only tables) — both were fixed in code, not by weakening the check.

## Known limitations

- No Supabase sign-in screen in the web app, so `AUTH_MODE=supabase` is wired but not
  end-to-end usable from the UI yet.
- No Telegram adapter, no encryption format, no uploads, previews, sharing, versions UI,
  PWA or offline queue. The schema for them exists; the code does not.
- PGlite is a development/test driver: a single connection, not for production traffic.
  Production must set `DATABASE_URL`.
- No Playwright end-to-end suite, CI pipeline or container images in this milestone.
- Theme is per browser (cookie) until a settings endpoint exists.
- Milestone 1 rate limits are global; per-route policies for uploads arrive with uploads.

## Next milestone entry criteria (Milestone 2 — metadata and UI)

1. `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/files`, `/api/v1/folders`, `/api/v1/tags`,
   `/api/v1/search` with schemas, pagination and owner-scoped queries.
2. File and folder CRUD, bulk actions, favorites, tags, sorting and filtering in the UI,
   with grid and list views.
3. Bento category cards (Images, Videos, Audio, Documents, APKs, Archives, Downloads,
   Other) backed by real aggregate queries.
4. TanStack Query introduced for client-side server state, with cache invalidation instead
   of full-library refreshes.
5. Loading, refreshing, empty and permission-denied states for each new screen; tests for
   both allowed and denied operations on every new endpoint.

Milestone 1 is complete, verified, and running. The API is on `127.0.0.1:8787`, the web app on `localhost:3000`, and sign-in works with any email address.

**What I built**

- **Monorepo** (`apps/api`, `apps/web`, `packages/contracts`) with strict TypeScript, validated env config, and a shared TypeBox contract package — see [package.json](package.json) and [contracts](packages/contracts/src/index.ts).
- **Database**: ten Supabase-compatible migrations in [supabase/migrations](supabase/migrations/0001_profiles_settings.sql) covering Part B — ownership-aware composite FKs, folder-cycle guard, immutable versions, current-version consistency trigger, all B4 indexes, RLS on every table with `anon` fully revoked, and a final migration that fails the run if RLS/grants/policy coverage regress. It caught two real defects while I was building it.
- **API**: [app.ts](apps/api/src/app.ts) composes JWT verification (dev HS256 + Supabase JWKS/secret), an auth preHandler, CORS, rate limits, `no-store` headers and the SRS error envelope; modules for [`/health`](apps/api/src/modules/health/routes.ts), [`/api/v1/me`](apps/api/src/modules/me/repository.ts), [`/api/v1/setup/status`](apps/api/src/modules/setup/repository.ts) and a production-disabled [`/api/v1/dev/session`](apps/api/src/modules/dev-auth/routes.ts).
- **Local-first database**: `DATABASE_URL` empty runs real PostgreSQL 17 (PGlite) at `apps/api/.data/pglite`; set it and the same SQL runs on Supabase through `pg`. No Docker or credentials needed — Docker Desktop's daemon wasn't available here, so this keeps setup a single command.
- **Web**: themed shell with Amber Minimal / Graphite Terminal (CSS-variable tokens, cookie-backed, no flash), httpOnly session cookie, protected `(app)` segment, sign-in/sign-out, bento dashboard reading live storage/setup/health data, and a settings page that states connection, vault and retention status honestly. Upcoming destinations are marked "Soon" rather than rendered as dead buttons.

**Verified**

`pnpm -r typecheck` passes for all three packages; `pnpm test` passes 44 tests (31 API + 15 RLS in `apps/api/test/rls.test.ts` running as the real `authenticated` role with `request.jwt.claims`, plus 13 web component/format tests); `next build` succeeds; and in the browser I confirmed the unauthenticated redirect, sign-in, dashboard data, theme switching (`aria-pressed` + computed colours), settings, sign-out clearing the session, and the 390 px layout with 56 px touch targets and no overflow.

**Known limits (by design, documented in [decisions](docs/architecture/decisions.md) and the [milestone report](docs/reports/milestone-1.md))**: no Telegram adapter, encryption format, uploads, previews, sharing or PWA yet; `AUTH_MODE=supabase` is wired server-side but there's no Supabase sign-in screen; PGlite is dev/test only. Setup steps and the Supabase switch are in [local-development.md](docs/setup/local-development.md).

/**
 * Apply every pending migration in filename order. Migrations are immutable:
 * re-running against a database whose recorded checksum differs fails loudly
 * instead of silently drifting.
 */
export async function runMigrations(
  db: Db,
  options: { localAuthStub: boolean; migrationsDir?: string },
): Promise<MigrationResult> {
  const dir = options.migrationsDir ?? MIGRATIONS_DIR;

  if (options.localAuthStub) {
    const stub = await readFile(LOCAL_AUTH_STUB_PATH, 'utf8');
    await db.exec(stub);
  }

  await db.exec(`
    create table if not exists public.schema_migrations (
      name text primary key,
      checksum text not null,
      applied_at timestamptz not null default now()
    );
    alter table public.schema_migrations enable row level security;
  `);

  const appliedRows = await db.query<{ name: string; checksum: string }>(
    'select name, checksum from public.schema_migrations',
  );
  const applied = new Map(appliedRows.rows.map((row) => [row.name, row.checksum]));

  const result: MigrationResult = { applied: [], skipped: [] };

  for (const name of await listMigrationFiles(dir)) {
    const sql = await readFile(path.join(dir, name), 'utf8');
    const digest = checksum(sql);
    const previous = applied.get(name);

    if (previous !== undefined) {
      if (previous !== digest) {
        throw new Error(
          `Migration ${name} was modified after being applied (checksum mismatch). ` +
            'Migrations are immutable; add a new migration instead.',
        );
      }
      result.skipped.push(name);
      continue;
    }

    await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.exec(sql);
      await tx.query(
        'insert into public.schema_migrations (name, checksum) values ($1, $2)',
        [name, digest],
      );
    });
    result.applied.push(name);
  }

  return result;
}

export function formatBytes(bytes: number): string {
  if (!Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes <= 0) {
    return '0 B';
  }

  let value = bytes;
  let unitIndex = 0;
  while (value >= 1024 && unitIndex < UNITS.length - 1) {
    value /= 1024;
    unitIndex += 1;
  }

  const digits = unitIndex === 0 || value >= 100 ? 0 : value >= 10 ? 1 : 2;
  return `${value.toFixed(digits)} ${UNITS[unitIndex]}`;
}

const pluralRules = new Intl.PluralRules('en-US');

export function formatCount(count: number, singular: string, plural = `${singular}s`): string {
  const word = pluralRules.select(count) === 'one' ? singular : plural;
  return `${count.toLocaleString('en-US')} ${word}`;
}

export function formatDateTime(value: string): string {
  const date = new Date(value);
  if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
    return 'Unknown';
  }
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
    dateStyle: 'medium',
    timeStyle: 'short',
    timeZone: 'UTC',
  }).format(date);
}

export function formatDuration(seconds: number): string {
  const total = Math.max(0, Math.floor(seconds));
  const hours = Math.floor(total / 3600);
  const minutes = Math.floor((total % 3600) / 60);
  if (hours > 0) return `${hours}h ${minutes}m`;
  if (minutes > 0) return `${minutes}m`;
  return `${total}s`;
}

 * cookie is the source of truth and no flash-of-wrong-theme can occur.

  return isTheme(value) ? value : 'amber';
}

  const store = await cookies();
  store.set(THEME_COOKIE, theme, {
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
    path: '/',
    maxAge: THEME_MAX_AGE_SECONDS,
  });

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  let config: ReturnType<typeof loadConfig>;
  try {

{"kind":"tool","id":"e2aEjZf3W6E","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"docs/architecture/encryption-format.md","instructions":"Write the pinned stackbase/1 encryption format specification (vault hierarchy, file format, manifest, validation rules, test vectors, threat notes).","content":"# StackBase encryption format — `stackbase/1`

**Status:** pinned (SRS A6, milestone 0 items "finalize the encryption format and test
vectors"). Any change to this document requires a new format version; both the vault and
every file version record the version they were written with, so old data stays readable.

The format is implemented **client-side only**, in the browser (`apps/web/src/lib/crypto`),
on top of the reviewed `libsodium-wrappers-sumo` build of libsodium. The server stores
opaque ciphertext, wrapped keys, non-secret parameters and hashes; it never receives the
passphrase, the vault key, the data keys or any plaintext.

## 1. Primitives

| Purpose | Primitive | libsodium API |
|---|---|---|
| Passphrase KDF | Argon2id13 | `crypto_pwhash` |
| Key wrapping / verifier | XSalsa20-Poly1305 (secretbox) | `crypto_secretbox_easy` / `crypto_secretbox_open_easy` |
| File content | XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretstream | `crypto_secretstream_xchacha20poly1305_{init_push,init_pull,push,pull}` |
| Hashing | SHA-256 | `crypto_hash_sha256_init/update/final` (incremental) |

No new construction is invented: every piece is a documented libsodium primitive with a
single, explicit composition described below.

## 2. Vault key hierarchy

1. **Vault key (VK)** — [… 4,546 characters omitted] x characters.
- Unknown fields are rejected (`additionalProperties: false`).

A manifest that fails validation is never stored, never attached to a version, and never
used for decryption.

## 5. What the server can and cannot do

| Server sees | Server cannot |
|---|---|
| Ciphertext bytes, sizes, chunk boundaries | Plaintext of any file |
| Wrapped data keys, wrapped vault key | Vault key or data keys |
| KDF parameters, salt, nonces, stream header | Passphrase, KEK |
| SHA-256 hashes (ciphertext, plaintext fingerprint) | Reverse the hashes |
| File names, sizes, MIME types, folders, tags (metadata) | Decrypt names inside content |

The server does verify **transfer integrity**: per-chunk SHA-256 checksums while receiving
and the full `ciphertextHash` after assembly. A mismatch is `UPLOAD_INTEGRITY_FAILED` and
the version is never created.

## 6. Test vectors

Deterministic vectors are committed in `apps/web/src/lib/crypto/test-vectors.ts` and
asserted by `apps/web/test/crypto-vectors.test.ts`:

- **Vault vector** — fixed passphrase, salt and parameters produce a pinned KEK; wrapping a
  pinned vault key with a pinned nonce produces pinned ciphertext that opens back.
- **File vector** — a fixed data key, stream header and nonce-independent content (the
  secretstream construction derives per-chunk nonces from its own state) encrypt a fixed
  3-chunk plaintext to a pinned ciphertext hash; decrypting the ciphertext reproduces the
  plaintext exactly.
- **Authenticity vectors** — flipping one ciphertext byte, reordering two chunks or
  truncating the stream must throw and produce no plaintext.

Any change that breaks a vector is a format change and must bump the version.

## 7. Accepted limitations

- The client holds the vault key in memory only; reloading the page locks the vault again.
  The passphrase is never persisted anywhere.

{"kind":"tool","id":"e58DytXkB2s","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/web/src/lib/api/proxy.ts","instructions":"Add the shared browser-facing proxy helpers used by Next route handlers.","content":"import {
  ApiRequestError,
  ApiUnavailableError,
  UnauthenticatedError,
  apiFetch,
} from './client';

/**
 * The session token lives in an httpOnly cookie, so the browser cannot talk to
 * the API directly. Every browser-initiated call (uploads, downloads, vault
 * creation) goes through a Next route handler, which attaches the token and
 * forwards the response — see ADR-018.
 */

const ERROR_HEADERS = { 'cache-control': 'no-store' } as const;

function errorResponse(error: unknown): Response {
  if (error instanceof UnauthenticatedError) {
    return Response.json(
      { error: { code: 'AUTH_REQUIRED', message: 'Sign in again to continue.' } },
      { status: 401, headers: ERROR_HEADERS },
    );
  }
  if (error instanceof ApiRequestError) {
    return Response.json(
      { error: { code: error.code, message: error.message } },
      { status: error.status, headers: ERROR_HEADERS },
    );
  }
  if (error instanceof ApiUnavailableError) {
    return Response.json(
      { error: { code: 'DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE', message: 'The API is unreachable.' } },
      { status: 502, headers: ERROR_HEADERS },
    );
  }
  return Response.json(
    { error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'The request could not be completed.' } },
    { status: 500, headers: ERROR_HEADERS },
  );
}

/** Forwards a JSON request/response pair to the API on behalf of the browser. */
export async function forwardJson(
  path: string,
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE',
  body?: unknown,
): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    const data = await apiFetch<unknown>(path, {
      method,
      ...(body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
    });
    return Response.json(data, { headers: ERROR_HEADERS });
  } catch (error) {
    return errorResponse(error);
  }
}

/** Forwards a binary request body (an encrypted chunk) to the API. */
export async function forwardBinary(
  path: string,
  method: 'PUT' | 'POST',
  body: ArrayBuffer,
  headers: Record<string, string>,
): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    const data = await apiFetch<unknown>(path, {
      method,
      body: new Uint8Array(body),
      headers,
    });
    return Response.json(data, { headers: ERROR_HEADERS });
  } catch (error) {
    return errorResponse(error);
  }
}

/** Maps a failed API response into the same error envelope the proxy uses. */
export async function responseError(response: Response): Promise<Response> {
  const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as
    | { error?: { code?: string; message?: string } }
    | null;
  return Response.json(
    {
      error: {
        code: body?.error?.code ?? 'INTERNAL_ERROR',
        message: body?.error?.message ?? 'The request could not be completed.',
      },
    },
    { status: response.status, headers: ERROR_HEADERS },
  );
}

export { errorResponse };

import { errorResponse, forwardBinary } from '@/lib/api/proxy';

interface Params {
  params: Promise<{ uploadId: string; chunkNumber: string }>;
}

/** One encrypted chunk; ciphertext only, bounds enforced by the API. */
export async function PUT(request: Request, { params }: Params): Promise<Response> {
  try {
    const { uploadId, chunkNumber } = await params;
    const checksum = request.headers.get(UPLOAD_CHUNK_CHECKSUM_HEADER);
    if (!checksum) {
      return Response.json(
        {
          error: {
            code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
            message: `The ${UPLOAD_CHUNK_CHECKSUM_HEADER} header is required.`,
          },
        },
        { status: 400 },
      );
    }

    const body = await request.arrayBuffer();
    return await forwardBinary(
      `/api/v1/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/chunks/${encodeURIComponent(chunkNumber)}`,
      'PUT',
      body,
      {
        'content-type': UPLOAD_CHUNK_CONTENT_TYPE,
        [UPLOAD_CHUNK_CHECKSUM_HEADER]: checksum,
      },
    );
  } catch (error) {
    return errorResponse(error);
  }
}

  sourceBytes: number;
}

  type CancelUploadResponse,
  type CreateUploadRequest,
  type CreateUploadResponse,
  type FileVersionListResponse,
  type FinalizeUploadRequest,
  type FinalizeUploadResponse,
  type UploadChunkResponse,
} from '@stackbase/contracts';
import type { UploadTransport } from './pipeline';

/**
 * Talks to this app's own route handlers (ADR-018), which attach the httpOnly
 * session cookie's token and forward to the API. Error bodies keep the API's
 * `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope, so the queue can show real reasons.
 */

export class UploadRequestError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly code: string;

  constructor(status: number, code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'UploadRequestError';
    this.status = status;
    this.code = code;
  }
}

async function toError(response: Response): Promise<UploadRequestError> {
  const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as
    | { error?: { code?: string; message?: string } }
    | null;
  return new UploadRequestError(
    response.status,
    body?.error?.code ?? 'INTERNAL_ERROR',
    body?.error?.message ?? 'The request failed.',
  );
}

async function sendJson<T>(path: string, method: 'GET' | 'POST', body?: unknown): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(path, {
    method,
    cache: 'no-store',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    ...(body === undefined ? {} : { body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw await toError(response);
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

export const uploadTransport: UploadTransport = {
  create: (body: CreateUploadRequest) => sendJson<CreateUploadResponse>('/api/uploads', 'POST', body),

  async putChunk(uploadId, chunkNumber, data, checksum) {
    const response = await fetch(
      `/api/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/chunks/${chunkNumber}`,
      {
        method: 'PUT',
        cache: 'no-store',
        headers: {
          'content-type': UPLOAD_CHUNK_CONTENT_TYPE,
          [UPLOAD_CHUNK_CHECKSUM_HEADER]: checksum,
        },
        body: data as unknown as BodyInit,
      },
    );
    if (!response.ok) throw await toError(response);
    return (await response.json()) as UploadChunkResponse;
  },

  finalize: (uploadId: string, body: FinalizeUploadRequest) =>
    sendJson<FinalizeUploadResponse>(
      `/api/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/finalize`,
      'POST',
      body,
    ),

  cancel: (uploadId: string) =>
    sendJson<CancelUploadResponse>(`/api/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/cancel`, 'POST'),

  listVersions: (fileId: string) =>
    sendJson<FileVersionListResponse>(
      `/api/files/${encodeURIComponent(fileId)}/versions`,
      'GET',
    ),
};

{"kind":"tool","id":"e6cIMe7kd5Q","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/web/src/lib/api/browser.ts","instructions":"Add the small browser-side fetch helper shared by upload, download and vault flows.","content":"/**
 * Browser → route handler helper. The token is an httpOnly cookie, so the
 * browser can only reach the API through this app's own handlers (ADR-018);
 * they keep the API's `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope intact, which is
 * what makes a real reason displayable in the UI.
 */

export class BrowserRequestError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly code: string;

  constructor(status: number, code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'BrowserRequestError';
    this.status = status;
    this.code = code;
  }
}

async function errorFrom(response: Response): Promise<BrowserRequestError> {
  const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as
    | { error?: { code?: string; message?: string } }
    | null;
  return new BrowserRequestError(
    response.status,
    body?.error?.code ?? 'INTERNAL_ERROR',
    body?.error?.message ?? 'The request failed.',
  );
}

export async function sendJson<T>(
  path: string,
  options: { method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE'; body?: unknown },
): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(path, {
    method: options.method,
    cache: 'no-store',
    ...(options.body === undefined
      ? {}
      : { headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(options.body) }),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw await errorFrom(response);
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

/** Raw response for streamed bodies; the caller owns reading and cancelling. */
export async function sendRaw(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> {
  const response = await fetch(path, { ...init, cache: 'no-store' });
  if (!response.ok) throw await errorFrom(response);
  return response;
}

export const isBrowserRequestError = (error: unknown): error is BrowserRequestError =>
  error instanceof BrowserRequestError;

/**
 * Talks to this app's own route handlers (ADR-018), which attach the httpOnly
 * session cookie's token and forward to the API. Chunk bodies stay binary the
 * whole way; only the metadata travels as JSON.
 */
export const uploadTransport: UploadTransport = {
  create: (body: CreateUploadRequest) =>
    sendJson<CreateUploadResponse>('/api/uploads', { method: 'POST', body }),

  async putChunk(uploadId, chunkNumber, data, checksum) {
    const response = await sendRaw(
      `/api/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/chunks/${chunkNumber}`,
      {
        method: 'PUT',
        headers: {
          'content-type': UPLOAD_CHUNK_CONTENT_TYPE,
          [UPLOAD_CHUNK_CHECKSUM_HEADER]: checksum,
        },
        body: data as unknown as BodyInit,
      },
    );
    return (await response.json()) as UploadChunkResponse;
  },

  finalize: (uploadId: string, body: FinalizeUploadRequest) =>
    sendJson<FinalizeUploadResponse>(`/api/uploads/${encodeURIComponent(uploadId)}/finalize`, {
      method: 'POST',
      body,

    }),

{"kind":"tool","id":"e6fMM9AsoWI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/web/src/features/encryption/vault-context.tsx","instructions":"Add the in-memory vault provider used by the app shell.","content":"'use client';

import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useMemo,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react';
import type { VaultRecord, VaultResponse } from '@stackbase/contracts';
import { CryptoError } from '@/lib/crypto/errors';
import { createVault as buildVault, unlockVault } from '@/lib/crypto/vault';
import { sendJson } from '@/lib/api/browser';

/**
 * Holds the vault key for the life of the page. It is deliberately React state
 * and nothing else: no cookie, no storage, no server round-trip. Reloading the
 * page locks the vault again, which is the documented trade-off of `stackbase/1`.
 */

export type VaultStatus = 'absent' | 'locked' | 'unlocked';

export interface VaultContextValue {
  record: VaultRecord | null;
  status: VaultStatus;
  /** Set only while unlocked; never serialised, never sent anywhere. */
  key: Uint8Array | null;
  create(passphrase: string): Promise<void>;
  unlock(passphrase: string): Promise<void>;
  lock(): void;
}

const VaultContext = createContext<VaultContextValue | null>(null);

export function VaultProvider({
  record: initialRecord,
  children,
}: {
  record: VaultRecord | null;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [record, setRecord] = useState<VaultRecord | null>(initialRecord);
  const [key, setKey] = useState<Uint8Array | null>(null);

  const create = useCallback(async (passphrase: string) => {
    const { request, vaultKey } = await buildVault(passphrase);
    const response = await sendJson<VaultResponse>('/api/encryption/vault', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: request,
    });
    setRecord(response.vault);
    setKey(vaultKey);
  }, []);

  const unlock = useCallback(
    async (passphrase: string) => {
      if (!record) {
        throw new CryptoError('WRONG_VAULT_KEY', 'No vault exists for this account yet.');
      }
      setKey(await unlockVault(record, passphrase));
    },
    [record],
  );

  const lock = useCallback(() => {
    setKey(null);
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo<VaultContextValue>(
    () => ({
      record,
      key,
      status: record === null ? 'absent' : key === null ? 'locked' : 'unlocked',
      create,
      unlock,
      lock,
    }),
    [create, key, lock, record, unlock],
  );

  return <VaultContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</VaultContext.Provider>;
}

export function useVault(): VaultContextValue {
  const value = useContext(VaultContext);
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error('useVault must be used inside a VaultProvider.');
  }
  return value;
}
"}}

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { KeyRound } from 'lucide-react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Dialog, FormError } from '@/components/ui/Dialog';
import { CRYPTO_ERROR_COPY, CryptoError } from '@/lib/crypto/errors';
import { MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH } from '@/lib/crypto/vault';
import { useVault } from './vault-context';

/**
 * Shown whenever an action needs the vault key: uploading, downloading or
 * opening the settings card while locked. Unlocking only ever happens here, in
 * the browser, against the record the server already holds.
 */
export function UnlockVaultDialog({
  open,
  onClose,
  onUnlocked,
}: {
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  onUnlocked: () => void;
}) {
  const vault = useVault();
  const [passphrase, setPassphrase] = useState('');
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (open) {
      setPassphrase('');
      setError(null);
      setPending(false);
    }
  }, [open]);

  const submit = async (): Promise<void> => {
    if (pending || passphrase.length === 0) return;
    setPending(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await vault.unlock(passphrase);
      onUnlocked();
    } catch (failure) {
      setError(
        failure instanceof CryptoError
          ? failure.message
          : 'The vault could not be unlocked on this device.',
      );
      setPending(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Dialog
      open={open}
      onClose={onClose}
      title="Unlock your vault"
      description="The vault key never leaves this device; unlocking derives it from your passphrase in the browser."
      footer={
        <>
          <Button type="button" variant="secondary" size="sm" onClick={onClose}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            type="button"
            size="sm"
            onClick={() => void submit()}
            disabled={pending || passphrase.length === 0}
          >
            {pending ? 'Unlocking…' : 'Unlock'}
          </Button>
        </>
      }
    >
      <form
        className="space-y-3"
        onSubmit={(event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          void submit();
        }}
      >
        <FormError message={error} />
        <label className="block">
          <span className="text-xs font-medium">Passphrase</span>
          <input
            type="password"
            autoFocus
            value={passphrase}
            onChange={(event) => setPassphrase(event.target.value)}
            autoComplete="current-password"
            className="mt-1.5 h-10 w-full rounded-xl border border-border bg-surface px-3 text-sm"
          />
        </label>
        <p className="flex items-start gap-1.5 text-[11px] leading-relaxed text-muted">
          <KeyRound className="mt-0.5 size-3.5 shrink-0" aria-hidden="true" />
          {CRYPTO_ERROR_COPY.WRONG_PASSPHRASE} There is no recovery server-side: a lost passphrase
          means the encrypted files stay unreadable.
        </p>
        <p className="text-[11px] text-muted">
          Deriving the key takes a moment: Argon2id is deliberately slow
          ({MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH}+ characters required).
        </p>
      </form>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

import { useCallback, useState } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { Dialog } from '@/components/ui/Dialog';
import { UnlockVaultDialog } from './unlock-dialog';
import { useVault } from './vault-context';

/**
 * Every content action (upload, download) needs the vault key. The gate runs the
 * action straight away when the vault is unlocked, asks for the passphrase when
 * it is locked, and points at Settings when no vault exists yet — so callers
 * never have to branch on vault state themselves.
 */
export function useVaultGate() {
  const vault = useVault();
  const [pending, setPending] = useState<(() => void) | null>(null);
  const [unlockOpen, setUnlockOpen] = useState(false);
  const [setupOpen, setSetupOpen] = useState(false);

  const requireUnlocked = useCallback(
    (action: () => void) => {
      if (vault.status === 'unlocked') {
        action();
        return;
      }
      setPending(() => action);
      if (vault.status === 'locked') setUnlockOpen(true);
      else setSetupOpen(true);
    },
    [vault.status],
  );

  const close = useCallback(() => {
    setUnlockOpen(false);
    setSetupOpen(false);
    setPending(null);
  }, []);

  const dialog = (
    <>
      <UnlockVaultDialog
        open={unlockOpen}
        onClose={close}
        onUnlocked={() => {
          const action = pending;
          close();
          action?.();
        }}
      />
      <Dialog
        open={setupOpen}
        onClose={close}
        title="Create a vault first"
        description="Encryption is mandatory: nothing is uploaded, and no metadata is described as stored, until a vault exists."
        footer={
          <Link
            href="/settings"
            className="inline-flex h-9 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-primary px-3 text-xs font-medium text-primary-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-primary/90"
          >
            Open settings
          </Link>
        }
      >
        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed text-muted">
          A vault is a passphrase-wrapped key that lives in your browser. Create it once from the
          encryption card in Settings, and every upload is encrypted on this device before it
          leaves it.
        </p>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );

  return { requireUnlocked, dialog, status: vault.status, Button };
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"e7H_QOZEmms","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/web/src/features/setup/storage-status.ts","instructions":"Update storage copy for the shipped storage pipeline and the local provider.","content":"import type { SetupStatusResponse } from '@stackbase/contracts';

export type StatusVariant = 'success' | 'muted' | 'warning' | 'danger';

export interface StorageStatusSummary {
  variant: StatusVariant;
  label: string;
  detail: string;
}

/**
 * Single source of truth for how connection state is described, shared by the
 * dashboard and settings so both always tell the same story. The two providers
 * are described differently on purpose: `local` keeps ciphertext on the API
 * host and is only ever valid outside production (ADR-015).
 */
export function describeStorage(storage: SetupStatusResponse['storage']): StorageStatusSummary {
  const local = storage.provider === 'local';

  switch (storage.status) {
    case 'connected':
      return local
        ? {
            variant: 'warning',
            label: 'Development storage',
            detail:
              'Ciphertext is written to the development filesystem provider on the API host. Set TELEGRAM_API_ID and TELEGRAM_API_HASH to store it in your own Telegram account instead.',
          }
        : {
            variant: 'success',
            label: 'Connected',
            detail: storage.accountIdentifier
              ? `Linked as ${storage.accountIdentifier}. Ciphertext is stored in Saved Messages.`
              : 'Linked. Ciphertext is stored in Saved Messages.',
          };
    case 'error':
      return {
        variant: 'danger',
        label: 'Needs attention',
        detail: storage.lastErrorCode
          ? `Last error: ${storage.lastErrorCode}. Reconnect from settings.`
          : 'The provider rejected the last operation. Reconnect from settings.',
      };
    case 'expired':
      return {
        variant: 'warning',
        label: 'Expired',
        detail: 'The Telegram session expired. Reconnect before uploading.',
      };
    case 'disconnected':
      return {
        variant: 'warning',
        label: 'Disconnected',
        detail: 'Storage was disconnected. Files remain, but transfers are paused until you reconnect.',
      };
    default:
      return {
        variant: 'muted',
        label: 'Not connected',
        detail:
          'Link your Telegram account in settings to store ciphertext in your own Saved Messages.',
      };
  }
}

 * Which in-browser preview a file can have (FR-08, C4). Classification runs on
 * the stored metadata only — nothing about the content is known until the

 * viewer. Everything else shows the generic unsupported-file view.

export type PreviewKind = 'image' | 'video' | 'audio' | 'pdf' | 'none';

const EXTENSION_KINDS: Record<string, PreviewKind> = {
  png: 'image',
  jpg: 'image',
  jpeg: 'image',
  gif: 'image',
  webp: 'image',
  avif: 'image',
  bmp: 'image',
  svg: 'image',
  mp4: 'video',
  webm: 'video',
  mov: 'video',
  m4v: 'video',
  ogv: 'video',
  mp3: 'audio',
  m4a: 'audio',
  wav: 'audio',
  ogg: 'audio',
  opus: 'audio',
  flac: 'audio',
  aac: 'audio',
  pdf: 'pdf',
};

const extensionOf = (name: string): string => {
  const index = name.lastIndexOf('.');
  return index >= 0 ? name.slice(index + 1).toLowerCase() : '';
};

export function previewKindFor(mimeType: string, fileName: string): PreviewKind {
  const mime = mimeType.toLowerCase().split(';')[0]?.trim() ?? '';
  if (mime.startsWith('image/')) return 'image';
  if (mime.startsWith('video/')) return 'video';
  if (mime.startsWith('audio/')) return 'audio';
  if (mime === 'application/pdf') return 'pdf';
  // Uploads of unknown type still classify by extension (octet-stream, etc.).
  if (mime === '' || mime === 'application/octet-stream' || mime === 'binary/octet-stream') {
    return EXTENSION_KINDS[extensionOf(fileName)] ?? 'none';
  }
  return 'none';
}

**Date:** 28 October 2026
**Scope:** SRS Part E, Milestone 4 (persistent upload jobs, chunk tracking with retry and
resume, source-file reselection, image/video/audio/PDF previews and storage insights).
Local-first variant retained: everything below runs with the `local` provider and no
external credentials; Telegram remains a configured alternative.

**Exit criterion:** *interrupted uploads recover safely and previews do not expose file
contents to the server.* Met and demonstrated in a browser (see "Manual browser
verification").

---

## Implemented behavior

**Durable queue (API)**

- `GET /api/v1/uploads` returns every unfinished job, newest first (limit 50), including
  `receivedChunkNumbers` so a resumed client never has to guess what the server holds.
- Reading the queue runs a stale-job sweep: a client-driven job (`queued`, `preparing`,
  `encrypting`, `transferring`, `retrying`) untouched for **2 minutes** becomes
  `needs_source_file`; a stalled `finalizing` job gets **15 minutes** because a provider
  transfer legitimately runs without chunk traffic, then becomes
  `reconciliation_required`. Paused jobs are never swept — pausing is not a crash.
- State machine endpoints: `POST /api/v1/uploads/:id/pause|resume|retry`.
  `pause` accepts any client-driven job; `resume` only  [… 9,082 characters omitted] erification used the development filesystem provider.
- **Source-file reselection after a refresh is by design, not optional.** A browser cannot
  retain a `File` handle across a reload, so a restored job waits for the original file
  (verified by its SHA-256 fingerprint). Pause/resume within the same tab keeps the handle
  and needs no reselection.
- **Previews buffer the decrypted file in memory** (bounded at 64 MiB) and use one object
  URL; there is no range/streamed media playback or thumbnail cache for very large media.
- Jobs run **one at a time**; there is no reordering or per-file priority UI yet.
- Stale thresholds (2 min / 15 min) are fixed in the repository rather than configurable.
- A provider rate-limit response (429) triggers the same exponential backoff as a network
  error, but the panel shows a generic retry message rather than a provider-specific
  flood-wait countdown.
- Insights only **reports** duplicate candidates; there is no "keep one copy" deletion
  action yet.
- No version-history UI, sharing, PWA/offline support or Supabase sign-in screen
  (Milestones 5–6).
- `STORAGE_PROVIDER=local` stays development-only, and PGlite remains a development/test
  driver (`DATABASE_URL` is required for production concurrency).

## Next milestone entry criteria (Milestone 5 — recovery and sharing)

1. Version history: list every version of a file (the read endpoint exists), pin/restore an
   older version as current without deleting ciphertext that retained versions reference,
   and show it in the file details dialog.
2. Trash and retention: a purge path that honors the configured retention and an explicit
   "delete permanently" flow, with restore already covered.
3. Share creation and revocation: owner-scoped share rows and endpoints referencing one
   immutable version, with revocation checked server-side on every access.
4. Share-specific key transfer: wrap the version's data key for a share so a recipient can
   decrypt without ever receiving the vault key, plus the read-only download view.
5. Audit events: append-only records for share create/revoke, trash/purge and version
   restore, readable only by the owner.
6. Tests for both allowed and denied operations, expiry and revocation, and a browser
   pass proving a revoked link stops working while already-downloaded copies remain.

Milestone 4 — **upload reliability and previews** — is complete and verified end to end. The exit criterion is met: interrupted uploads recover safely, and previews never expose file contents to the server.

**What the verification actually proved**

- Fresh sign-in → vault created in Settings → badge *Unlocked*.
- A 152-byte PNG uploaded through the library: encrypted in the tab, streamed, finalized; the stored object is exactly **193 bytes** (24-byte header + 152 + 17 tag), with **zero staging files** left.
- Opening that file's details decrypted the stored ciphertext to a local `blob:` URL and rendered the image at its real 64×64 size.
- After a full page reload, a deliberately unfinished job reappeared in the queue as *"interrupted-notes.txt — 0 of 1 chunks already stored. Choose the file again to resume."* with **Choose file** and no misleading Retry.
- Pause → resume → cancel through the browser returned `200` with `paused` → `retrying` → `cancelled`; after cancelling, a reload showed an empty queue.
- Insights showed real totals (1 file / 152 B / 1 version). Uploading a second copy of the same bytes produced *"2 copies of 152 B · 152 B wasted"* from the client-declared plaintext fingerprint.

**Two real bugs surfaced by that run, now fixed**

1. Queue restore was impossible from the browser: there was no `GET /api/uploads` route handler (405), and no pause/resume/retry proxies. Added in [route.ts](apps/web/src/app/api/uploads/route.ts) and three new route files under `[uploadId]/`.
2. `apiFetch` sent `content-type: application/json` on bodyless POSTs; Fastify rejected the empty body, so cancel/pause/resume/retry failed with 500. [client.ts](apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts) now declares the header only when a body exists.

**Checks run**

- `pnpm typecheck` — pass (contracts, API, web), after the fixes.
- API suite — **140/140** across 14 files, including the 12 queue and 6 insights tests.
- Web suite — **75/75** across 9 files, re-run after the fixes.
- Production build — pass; the new proxy routes register as dynamic routes.

The full write-up is in [milestone-4.md](docs/reports/milestone-4.md), linked from the README, and [local-development.md](docs/setup/local-development.md) gained two troubleshooting entries learned during the run. Nothing was committed.

**Environment notes**

The pre-existing local PGlite database could not open after the abrupt restart (`RuntimeError: Aborted()`). I left it untouched at `apps/api/.data/pglite.corrupt-20261028` and verified against a separate data directory, then removed that temporary directory and rebuilt a clean, fully migrated database with `pnpm db:reset`. The verification servers are stopped; start them with `pnpm dev:api` and `pnpm dev:web`, and open **http://localhost:3000** — Next 16 blocks its dev client assets on `127.0.0.1`, which leaves the page non-interactive.

Remaining limitations are documented: Telegram was not exercised against a real account, previews buffer up to 64 MiB, restored jobs require reselecting the source file by design, and version history, sharing and PWA are still ahead.

The natural next step is Milestone 5.

-- Milestone 5: share-specific key transfer (SRS A7.2).
--
-- A share never exposes the vault key. When the owner creates the link, the
-- browser unwraps the version's data key with the vault key and re-wraps it
-- under a fresh random share key; only that wrapped key is stored here. The
-- share key itself travels in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to
-- the server, so the API can serve the ciphertext but cannot decrypt it.
--
-- Nullable for deployments that inserted rows before sharing existed; such rows
-- cannot be opened and the public endpoint refuses them with
-- SHARE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE. Every row created by the application is populated.

alter table public.shares
  add column wrapped_key jsonb,
  add constraint shares_wrapped_key_object check (
    wrapped_key is null or jsonb_typeof(wrapped_key) = 'object'
  );

comment on column public.shares.wrapped_key is
  'The shared version''s data key wrapped under the URL-fragment share key '
  '(xsalsa20poly1305). Not a secret on its own, but useless without the fragment.';

comment on table public.shares is
  'Revocable share of one immutable file version. Only token_hash is stored; the '
  'raw token lives with the recipient. Revocation cannot erase copies already '
  'downloaded. download_count must be incremented atomically.';

/**
 * Append-only audit trail (FR-13). Callers pass no secrets: no raw share token,
 * password, key, plaintext or Telegram session material ever reaches this
 * module. Writes run inside the caller's transaction where the action and its
 * audit record must succeed or fail together.

export interface AuditInput {
  eventType: string;
  resourceType?: string | null;
  resourceId?: string | null;
  result?: AuditResult;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export async function recordAuditEvent(
  db: Db | Queryable,
  userId: string,
  input: AuditInput,
): Promise<void> {
  await db.query(
    `insert into public.audit_events
       (user_id, event_type, resource_type, resource_id, result, event_metadata)
     values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6::jsonb)`,
    [
      userId,
      input.eventType,
      input.resourceType ?? null,
      input.resourceId ?? null,
      input.result ?? 'success',
      JSON.stringify(input.metadata ?? {}),
    ],
  );
}

interface AuditRow {
  id: string;
  eventType: string;
  resourceType: string | null;
  resourceId: string | null;
  result: string;
  metadata: unknown;
  createdAt: unknown;
}

export async function listAuditEvents(
  db: Db,
  userId: string,
  limit: number,
): Promise<AuditEvent[]> {
  const { rows } = await db.query<AuditRow>(
    `select id,
            event_type as "eventType",
            resource_type as "resourceType",
            resource_id as "resourceId",
            result,
            event_metadata as metadata,
            created_at as "createdAt"
       from public.audit_events
      where user_id = $1
      order by created_at desc, id desc
      limit $2`,
    [userId, limit],
  );

  return rows.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id,
    eventType: row.eventType,
    resourceType: row.resourceType,
    resourceId: row.resourceId,
    result: row.result as AuditEvent['result'],
    metadata:
      typeof row.metadata === 'object' && row.metadata !== null
        ? (row.metadata as Record<string, unknown>)
        : {},
    createdAt: toIsoString(row.createdAt),
  }));

import { useState } from 'react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';
import type { Share, ShareStatus } from '@stackbase/contracts';
import { ShieldOff } from 'lucide-react';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/Badge';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/Button';
import { FormError } from '@/components/ui/Dialog';
import { sendJson } from '@/lib/api/browser';
import { formatDateTime } from '@/lib/utils/format';

const STATUS_VARIANT: Record<ShareStatus, 'success' | 'muted' | 'warning' | 'danger'> = {
  active: 'success',
  expired: 'muted',
  revoked: 'danger',
  exhausted: 'warning',
};

/**
 * All links owned by the account. The raw link is deliberately absent: only its
 * token hash is stored, so management offers status and revocation, not a
 * recoverable URL (ADR-019).
 */
export function ShareList({ shares }: { shares: readonly Share[] }) {
  const router = useRouter();
  const [revokingId, setRevokingId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const revoke = async (share: Share): Promise<void> => {
    setRevokingId(share.id);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await sendJson(`/api/shares/${encodeURIComponent(share.id)}/revoke`, { method: 'POST' });
      router.refresh();
    } catch (failure) {
      setError(failure instanceof Error ? failure.message : 'The link could not be revoked.');
    } finally {
      setRevokingId(null);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <FormError message={error} />

      <ul className="divide-y divide-border overflow-hidden rounded-card border border-border bg-surface">
        {shares.map((share) => (
          <li
            key={share.id}
            className="flex flex-col gap-3 px-4 py-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center"
          >
            <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
              <p className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 text-sm font-medium">
                <span className="truncate">{share.fileName}</span>
                <Badge variant={STATUS_VARIANT[share.status]}>{share.status}</Badge>
              </p>
              <p className="mt-0.5 text-[11px] text-muted">
                Version {share.versionNumber} · read-only ·{' '}
                {share.expiresAt ? `expires ${formatDateTime(share.expiresAt)}` : 'no expiry'} ·{' '}
                {share.downloadCount}
                {share.maxDownloads === null ? '' : `/${share.maxDownloads}`} downloads
              </p>
              <p className="mt-0.5 text-[11px] text-muted">
                Created {formatDateTime(share.createdAt)} · key travels in the link fragment,
                never to the server
              </p>
            </div>

            <Button
              type="button"
              variant="ghost"
              size="sm"
              className="self-start text-error hover:bg-error/10 sm:self-auto"
              disabled={share.status === 'revoked' || revokingId === share.id}
              onClick={() => void revoke(share)}
            >
              <ShieldOff className="size-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />
              {revokingId === share.id ? 'Revoking…' : 'Revoke'}
            </Button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <p className="text-[11px] leading-relaxed text-muted">
        A link can only be copied when it is created. Revocation stops future downloads through
        StackBase; it cannot erase copies a recipient already saved.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
"}}

{"kind":"tool","id":"gKqQkdSN5k4","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/web/src/app/s/[token]/page.tsx","instructions":"Add the public share page with explicit refusal states","content":"import type { PublicShare } from '@stackbase/contracts';
import { Ban, Clock3, Link2Off, ShieldAlert } from 'lucide-react';
import { Card } from '@/components/ui/Card';
import { PublicShareView } from '@/features/shares/public-share-view';
import { ApiRequestError, apiFetchPublic } from '@/lib/api/client';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

const REFUSAL: Record<string, { title: string; message: string }> = {
  SHARE_NOT_FOUND: {
    title: 'This link is not valid',
    message: 'No share matches this address. Check that the whole link was copied correctly.',
  },
  SHARE_REVOKED: {
    title: 'This link was revoked',
    message: 'The owner stopped sharing this file. Ask them for a new link if you still need it.',
  },
  SHARE_EXPIRED: {
    title: 'This link expired',
    message: 'The owner set an expiry date and it has passed. Ask them for a fresh link.',
  },
  SHARE_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_REACHED: {
    title: 'Download limit reached',
    message: 'This link only allowed a fixed number of downloads, and they have all been used.',
  },
  SHARE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE: {
    title: 'This file is no longer available',
    message: 'The owner deleted this file, so its share cannot be opened.',
  },
  STORAGE_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED: {
    title: 'This file is temporarily unavailable',
    message: 'The owner’s storage provider does not currently have a verified copy. Try later.',
  },
};

export default async function PublicSharePage({
  params,
}: {
  params: Promise<{ token: string }>;
}) {
  const { token } = await params;

  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) {
    return <Refusal title={REFUSAL.SHARE_NOT_FOUND.title} message={REFUSAL.SHARE_NOT_FOUND.message} />;
  }

  let view: PublicShare;
  try {
    view = await apiFetchPublic<PublicShare>(
      `/api/v1/public/shares/${encodeURIComponent(token)}`,
    );
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ApiRequestError) {
      const copy = REFUSAL[error.code] ?? {
        title: 'This link cannot be opened',
        message: error.message,
      };
      return <Refusal title={copy.title} message={copy.message} />;
    }
    throw error;
  }

  return <PublicShareView token={token} initialView={view} />;
}

function Refusal({ title, message }: { title: string; message: string }) {
  const Icon =
    title === 'This link expired'
      ? Clock3
      : title === 'This link was revoked'
        ? Ban
        : title === 'This link is not valid'
          ? Link2Off
          : ShieldAlert;

  return (
    <Card className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
        <span className="grid size-11 shrink-0 place-items-center rounded-2xl bg-error/10 text-error">
          <Icon className="size-5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </span>
        <div>
          <h1 className="text-lg font-semibold leading-tight">{title}</h1>
          <p className="mt-1.5 text-sm leading-relaxed text-muted">{message}</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </Card>
  );
}
"}}

+-- 0013_share_wrapped_keys.sql
+-- Milestone 5: share-specific key transfer (SRS A7.2).
+--
+-- A share never exposes the vault key. When the owner creates the link, the
+-- browser unwraps the version's data key with the vault key and re-wraps it
+-- under a fresh random share key; only that wrapped key is stored here. The
+-- share key itself travels in the URL fragment, which browsers never send to
+-- the server, so the API can serve the ciphertext but cannot decrypt it.
+--
+-- Nullable for deployments that inserted rows before sharing existed; such rows
+-- cannot be opened and the public endpoint refuses them with
+-- SHARE_KEY_UNAVAILABLE. Every row created by the application is populated.
+
+alter table public.shares
+  add column wrapped_key jsonb,
+  add constraint shares_wrapped_key_object check (
+    wrapped_key is null or jsonb_typeof(wrapped_key) = 'object'
+  );
+
+comment on column public.shares.wrapped_key is
+  'The shared version''s data key wrapped under the URL-fragment share key '
+  '(xsalsa20poly1305). Not a secret on its own, but useless without the fragment.';
+
+comment on table public.shares is
+  'Revocable share of one immutable file version. Only token_hash is stored; the '
+  'raw token lives with the recipient. Revocation cannot erase copies already '
+  'downloaded. download_count must be incremented atomically.';

  '^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$';

});

/** Recovery (FR-11): append a new version pointing at an old version's content. */
export function registerVersionRestoreRoutes(

  deps: { db: Db },
): void {
  app.post<{ Params: VersionParamsType }>(
    '/api/v1/files/:fileId/versions/:versionId/restore',

      return restoreFileVersion(
        deps.db,
        user.id,
        request.params.fileId,
        request.params.versionId,
      );
    },
  );
}

export type ActionResult<T = undefined> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; message: string };

import { cookies } from 'next/headers';

/**
 * The access token lives in an httpOnly cookie so no script (including any
 * preview/third-party code) can read it. It is only ever attached by the server
 * when talking to the API.
 */
const SESSION_COOKIE = 'stackbase_session';

export async function getSessionToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  const store = await cookies();
  return store.get(SESSION_COOKIE)?.value ?? null;
}

export async function setSessionCookie(token: string, expiresAt: string): Promise<void> {
  const store = await cookies();
  store.set(SESSION_COOKIE, token, {
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: 'lax',
    secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
    path: '/',
    expires: new Date(expiresAt),
  });
}

export async function clearSessionCookie(): Promise<void> {
  const store = await cookies();
  store.delete(SESSION_COOKIE);
}

A self-hostable personal cloud drive. Metadata lives in PostgreSQL (Supabase-compatible),

Milestone 6's security/integration/end-to-end sweep is done, and it turned up one real bug.

**What the sweep proves**

[security-sweep.test.ts](apps/api/test/security-sweep.test.ts) takes the *real* route table from `app.printRoutes()` rather than a hand-written list, so it cannot drift: a route added without `preHandler: app.authenticate` fails the suite (an unknown route throws "add a schema-valid request"). # FINAL IMPLEMENTATION RULES

1. Treat this document as the authoritative specification.
2. Inspect the existing repository before changing its structure.
3. Do not implement all milestones in one unreviewed change.
4. Use reviewed cryptographic libraries and a versioned format.

import type { FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import {
  DevSessionRequestSchema,
  DevSessionResponseSchema,
  type DevSessionRequest,
  type DevSessionResponse,
} from '@stackbase/contracts';
import type { Db } from '../../database/db';
import type { Config } from '../../config/env';
import { issueDevSessionToken } from '../../security/token';

interface DevAuthDeps {
  db: Db;
  auth: Extract<Config['auth'], { mode: 'dev' }>;
}

/**
 * Local-first development sign-in. Registered only when AUTH_MODE=dev and the
 * process is not production; a real deployment uses Supabase Auth.
 */
export function registerDevAuthRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, deps: DevAuthDeps): void {
  app.post(
    '/api/v1/dev/session',
    {
      schema: {
        body: DevSessionRequestSchema,
        response: { 200: DevSessionResponseSchema },
      },
      config: { rateLimit: { max: 20, timeWindow: '1 minute' } },
    },
    async (request) => {
      // The body schema above has already validated this shape at runtime.
      const { email: rawEmail } = request.body as DevSessionRequest;
      const email = rawEmail.trim().toLowerCase();

      const userId = await deps.db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const existing = await tx.query<{ id: string }>(
          'select id from auth.users where lower(email) = $1',
          [email],
        );
        const found = existing.rows[0];
        if (found) {
          await tx.query('update auth.users set last_sign_in_at = now() where id = $1', [
            found.id,
          ]);
          return found.id;
        }

        const inserted = await tx.query<{ id: string }>(
          'insert into auth.users (email, last_sign_in_at) values ($1, now()) returning id',
          [email],
        );
        const created = inserted.rows[0];
        if (!created) {
          throw new Error('Failed to create development identity.');
        }
        return created.id;
      });

      const { accessToken, expiresAt } = await issueDevSessionToken(deps.auth, {
        userId,
        email,
      });

      const body: DevSessionResponse = {
        accessToken,
        tokenType: 'Bearer',
        expiresAt,
        user: { id: userId, email },
      };
      return body;
    },
  );
}

+// Scratch harness for clean-deployment validation. Runs only inside the
+// throwaway clone: serves a JWKS and mints RS256 tokens with the private key,
+// so the API's Supabase Auth verification path can be exercised without a
+// Supabase project.
+import { createServer } from 'node:http';
+import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { SignJWT, exportJWK, generateKeyPair } from 'jose';
+
+const subject = process.argv[2];
+const issuer = 'https://demo.stackbase.test/auth/v1';
+
+const { publicKey, privateKey } = await generateKeyPair('RS256');
+const { publicKey: otherPublic, privateKey: otherPrivate } = await generateKeyPair('RS256');
+void otherPublic;
+
+const jwk = { ...(await exportJWK(publicKey)), kid: 'sim-key-1', alg: 'RS256', use: 'sig' };
+
+const server = createServer((request, response) => {
+  response.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json' });
+  response.end(JSON.stringify({ keys: [jwk] }));
+});
+server.listen(8791, '127.0.0.1');
+
+const mint = (options = {}) =>
+  new SignJWT({ email: 'demo@stackbase.local', role: 'authenticated', ...(options.claims ?? {}) })
+    .setProtectedHeader({ alg: 'RS256', kid: 'sim-key-1' })
+    .setSubject(options.sub ?? subject)
+    .setIssuer(options.iss ?? issuer)
+    .setAudience(options.aud ?? 'authenticated')
+    .setIssuedAt()
+    .setExpirationTime(options.exp ?? '1h')
+    .sign(options.key ?? privateKey);
+
+const tokens = {
+  valid: await mint(),
+  expired: await mint({ exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - 120 }),
+  wrongAudience: await mint({ aud: 'some-other-app' }),
+  wrongIssuer: await mint({ iss: 'https://evil.example.com/auth/v1' }),
+  wrongKey: await mint({ key: otherPrivate }),
+  unknownSubject: await mint({ sub: '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000' }),
+};
+
+writeFileSync(new URL('./tokens.json', import.meta.url), JSON.stringify(tokens, null, 2));
+console.log('sim ready: jwks on http://127.0.0.1:8791/jwks.json');

import type { FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import type { Static } from '@sinclair/typebox';
import { MeResponseSchema, UserSettingsSchema, UserSettingsUpdateSchema } from '@stackbase/contracts';
import type { Db } from '../../database/db';
import { authRequired } from '../../errors';
import { getMe, updateUserSettings } from './repository';

export function registerMeRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, deps: { db: Db }): void {
  app.get(
    '/api/v1/me',
    {
      preHandler: app.authenticate,
      schema: { response: { 200: MeResponseSchema } },
    },
    async (request) => {
      const user = request.user;
      if (!user) {
        throw authRequired();
      }
      return getMe(deps.db, user);
    },
  );

  app.patch<{ Body: Static<typeof UserSettingsUpdateSchema> }>(
    '/api/v1/me/settings',
    {
      preHandler: app.authenticate,
      schema: {
        body: UserSettingsUpdateSchema,
        response: { 200: UserSettingsSchema },
      },
    },
    async (request) => {
      const user = request.user;
      if (!user) throw authRequired();
      return updateUserSettings(deps.db, user.id, request.body);
    },
  );
}

        store: store,
        isDebug: config.isDebug,
      );
    case null:

{"kind":"tool","id":"jcJj02-aAgM","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"apps/mobile/lib/core/ui/formatters.dart","content":"import 'package:intl/intl.dart';

String formatBytes(int bytes) {
  if (bytes <= 0) return '0 B';
  const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB'];
  var value = bytes.toDouble();
  var unit = 0;
  while (value >= 1024 && unit < units.length - 1) {
    value /= 1024;
    unit++;
  }
  final digits = value >= 100 || unit == 0 ? 0 : 1;
  return '${value.toStringAsFixed(digits)} ${units[unit]}';
}

String formatDate(DateTime value) {
  final local = value.toLocal();
  final now = DateTime.now();
  final sameDay =
      local.year == now.year &&
      local.month == now.month &&
      local.day == now.day;
  if (sameDay) return 'Today, ${DateFormat.Hm().format(local)}';
  return DateFormat.yMMMd().format(local);
}

String initialsFor(String? displayName, String? email) {
  final source = (displayName ?? email ?? '').trim();
  if (source.isEmpty) return '?';
  final parts = source.split(RegExp(r'[\s@._-]+')).where((p) => p.isNotEmpty);
  if (parts.isEmpty) return source.characters.first.toUpperCase();
  final first = parts.first.characters.first;
  final last = parts.length > 1 ? parts.elementAt(1).characters.first : '';
  return '$first$last'.toUpperCase();
}
